candidate_sentence_map.S1: Nordic Fibreboard AS reported a challenging 2025, with revenue declining 3.4% to €7.328 million from €7.592 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Fibreboard production and sales accounted for virtually all revenue at €7.325 million, while real estate management revenue fell to €3 thousand from €25 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Sales within the European Union, representing 92% of total revenue, remained relatively stable, but sales to Africa, Asia and the Middle East declined.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: EBITDA was negative €420 thousand, compared with negative €25 thousand in 2024, reducing the EBITDA margin to negative 6% from 0%.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: The fibreboard segment moved from positive EBITDA of €26 thousand to negative €296 thousand, primarily because of underutilized production capacity and the December factory shutdown.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: The shutdown was planned in 2025 to facilitate the transition to a new gas boiler house; personnel, maintenance and repair costs continued during the stoppage and had an approximately €0.2 million negative effect on fibreboard EBITDA.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: The real estate segment’s EBITDA loss also widened from €48 thousand to €86 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Gross profit declined to €603 thousand from €771 thousand, while distribution costs increased to €982 thousand from €935 thousand and administrative expenses rose to €502 thousand from €381 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Consequently, the operating loss widened to €940 thousand from €547 thousand, and the operating margin declined to negative 13% from negative 7%.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: After net financial costs of €214 thousand, the Group recorded a net loss of €1.154 million, compared with €786 thousand in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Basic and diluted loss per share improved to €0.14 from €0.17, reflecting the increase in shares following the October 2025 issue, although book value per share declined to €0.53 from €0.80.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Total assets increased to €9.323 million from €8.252 million, mainly due to investment in production assets and higher inventories.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Equity rose to €4.462 million from €3.616 million after a €2 million share issue, partly offset by the annual loss.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Borrowings declined to €3.168 million from €3.724 million, but year-end cash fell to €5 thousand from €53 thousand.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Operating cash flow was negative €503 thousand, compared with negative €174 thousand in 2024, while investing outflows increased to €989 thousand, including €1.367 million invested in production assets.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: The Group ended the year with negative working capital of €2.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Key developments included completion of the merger with Pärnu Riverside Development OÜ, continued development of the Admirali Quarter project, and major investment in a new gas boiler house, completed in January 2026.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: A preliminary agreement to sell ten Admirali Quarter properties was signed in January 2026.

evaluation.label: Yes
evaluation.justification: All key information units are adequately represented in the candidate summary. K1 is covered by S1, S2, and S3 (sales decline, EU stability, Africa/Asia drop, real estate revenue). K2 is covered by S4, S5, S6, S7, and S11 (EBITDA deterioration, net loss widening, causes including underutilized capacity and planned shutdown). K3 is covered by S13, S14, and S15 (asset increase, current assets, liabilities, equity). K4 is covered by S11 and S16 (cash flows from operations, investing, financing). K5 is covered by S2, S6, and S8 (revenue and EBITDA split between fibreboard and real estate). K6 is covered by S18 (merger completion and Admirali Quarter development). K7 is covered by S19 (preliminary sale agreement signed post-period). No material omissions affect overall understanding.
